question: Do several commands in one Member session share ONE backend PTY, or does each command spawn?
initiation: the Member's own model turn: the mock issued two sequential `bash` calls
commands: echo "A5SF_PTY_RUN=1"; echo "A5SF_PTY_PID=$$"; echo "A5SF_PTY_PS=$(ps -o pid=,sess=,tty=,ppid= -p $$ | tr -s " ")"; echo "A5SF_PTY_FD0=$(readlink /proc/$$/fd/0)"; echo "A5SF_PTY_CWD=$(pwd)"
echo "A5SF_PTY_RUN=2"; echo "A5SF_PTY_PID=$$"; echo "A5SF_PTY_PS=$(ps -o pid=,sess=,tty=,ppid= -p $$ | tr -s " ")"; echo "A5SF_PTY_FD0=$(readlink /proc/$$/fd/0)"; echo "A5SF_PTY_CWD=$(pwd)"

control.command: echo "A5SF_PTY_RUN=2C"; echo "A5SF_PTY_PID=$$"; echo "A5SF_PTY_PS=$(ps -o pid=,sess=,tty=,ppid= -p $$ | tr -s " ")"; echo "A5SF_PTY_FD0=$(readlink /proc/$$/fd/0)"; echo "A5SF_PTY_CWD=$(pwd)"
control.purpose: a second Member on the SAME World: if the two Members shared one shell, "same pid" would be a global fact rather than a per-Member one

limits.note: same pid/session/tty is PTY identity, not process-tree confinement; the shell is the legacy persistent shell the preset mounts
